basic_information.short_title: General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, FY 2026
basic_information.official_title: AN ACT APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE OPERATION OF THE BANGSAMORO GOVERNMENT FROM JANUARY ONE TO DECEMBER THIRTY-ONE, TWO THOUSAND TWENTY-SIX AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: The region's ₱114.08 billion budget for 2026 — the annual law that funds every ministry, office and commission, and sets the rules on how public money may be spent.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The Bangsamoro Government requires an annual appropriations act to operate. This one covers 1 January to 31 December 2026 and was themed 'Building a Future-Ready Bangsamoro'.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: ₱114,077,644,141.90 is appropriated from the block grant, other national subsidies, the region's share of national taxes collected in its territory, its own regional taxes and fees, and unutilised prior years' appropriations. The act also carries 83 sections of general provisions governing procurement, personnel benefits, savings, transparency and the use of funds.
who_will_be_affected: Everyone in the region, through the ministries and services this funds
All Bangsamoro Government personnel, whose allowances and bonuses it sets
Employees in the Sulu provincial offices, whose salaries it continues to fund transitionally
Contractors and suppliers, through procurement and transparency rules
Constituent LGUs, whose share of taxes does not lapse
Women's programmes, guaranteed at least 5% of every agency budget
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force from 1 January 2026. Appropriations are releasable and obligable until 31 December 2027, with Personnel Services expiring 31 December 2026.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. ₱114.08 billion for 2026. Beyond the money, this act carries the operating rules: at least 5% of every agency's budget for gender programmes, a ban on spending public funds on partisan activities, geo-tagged photos of every infrastructure project published online, and automatic salary suspension for officials who don't report.
in_practice: Funded from the annual block grant, other national subsidies, the region's share of national taxes collected in its territory, regional taxes, fees and charges, and unutilised prior years' appropriations
The Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament receives ₱7,257,475,847 — 6.4% of the budget
Personnel Services across the whole government may not exceed 45% of total revenue sources
At least 5% of every agency's budget goes to a Gender and Development Plan
Funding for partisan activities, including voters education programmes, is prohibited and any such appropriation is reverted
Agencies must publish geo-tagged photos of completed and ongoing infrastructure projects on their websites
Rainwater collection systems are required in public markets, school sites and government buildings
Appropriations run to 31 December 2027; the constituent LGUs' share of taxes does not lapse at all
Procurement runs through the New Government Procurement Act and PhilGEPS

for_specific_groups.Government employees: PERA of ₱2,000 a month, a uniform allowance up to ₱7,000 a year, a medical allowance up to ₱7,000 a year for HMO-type benefits, a mid-year bonus of 1 month's salary, a year-end bonus of 1 month plus a ₱5,000 cash gift — and deductions may never reduce monthly net take-home pay below ₱5,000.
for_specific_groups.Senior officials: Monthly representation and transportation allowances of ₱15,500 for the Chief Minister, ₱12,500 for Deputy Chief Ministers, the Speaker and Members of Parliament, ₱10,000 for Ministers, ₱9,500 for Deputy Ministers and Directors-General, ₱8,500 for Directors II and III, and ₱6,000 for Division Chiefs and Directors I. Annual extraordinary expenses run from ₱264,000 for the Chief Minister down to ₱19,200 for a Director II, plus ₱90,000 in miscellaneous expenses per office.
for_specific_groups.Government lawyers: A special counsel allowance of ₱5,000 for each court appearance, capped at 50% of monthly basic salary, and not payable for appearances before quasi-judicial or administrative agencies.
for_specific_groups.Employees in Sulu: Section 29 continues funding the salaries of personnel in the Sulu provincial offices as an institutional arrangement for seamless transition, following Executive Order No. 91 declaring the Province of Sulu part of Region IX (Zamboanga Peninsula) — until a permanent funding mechanism is established or the fiscal year ends, whichever comes first. The funds may also cover their retirement benefits and separation incentives.
for_specific_groups.Hospitals and health facilities: You retain your income but must remit 20% of what provincial, district and municipal hospitals, blood service facilities and laboratories generate to the Bangsamoro Treasury, with the retained portion used to augment operating and capital requirements.
for_specific_groups.Constituent LGUs: Your share of taxes, fees and charges collected within the region remains available until fully released, obligated and disbursed — it does not lapse with the rest of the budget.
for_specific_groups.Women: Every agency must formulate a Gender and Development Plan integrated into its regular activities and amounting to at least 5% of its budget, with plans and accomplishment reports going to the Bangsamoro Women Commission, which passes the data to the Philippine Commission on Women.
for_specific_groups.Persons with disabilities and senior cit: Agencies must formulate plans addressing your concerns, and all government infrastructure must provide architectural features enhancing your mobility, safety and welfare.
for_specific_groups.Contractors: Project title, location, description, the estimates behind the approved budget, and the winning contractor with its bid estimates must be published within 30 days of contract signing; actual cost and variation orders within 30 days of completion.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: All ministries, offices and agencies of the Bangsamoro Government, and its constituent local government units through their statutory shares.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: From 1 January 2026. Obligation runs to 31 December 2027 and infrastructure completion to 30 June 2028.
what_you_can_do: Check agency websites for geo-tagged photos of infrastructure projects and for the published cost of completed work
Look up procurement notices on PhilGEPS, designated the primary channel for all Bangsamoro Government procurement
Check the Bangsamoro Treasury Office's published list of all Special Accounts and funds, including their legal basis and allowable uses
Ask your agency for its Gender and Development Plan and accomplishment report
If reports are missing, Section 78 automatically suspends the responsible officials' salaries until they comply
watch_out_for: The Parliament's own appropriation is ₱7.26 billion — 6.4% of the entire regional budget — including a ₱1.97 billion Representation Program and a ₱480 million Constituency Servicing Program.
The Chief Minister is authorised to create new offices, modify the organisational structure of executive agencies, and create or modify positions whenever public interest requires.
Both the Chief Minister and the Speaker may declare and use savings within their respective appropriations, reporting to Parliament twice a year.
The act was passed and approved on the same day, 16 December 2025.

key_terms_explained.GAAB: General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro — the region's annual budget law. On effectivity it doubles as the allotment order authorising agencies to obligate funds.
key_terms_explained.Block grant: The annual transfer from the National Government that funds most of the regional budget.
key_terms_explained.Savings: Balances left unobligated because a project finished, was discontinued, or was delivered more cheaply. Money left unobligated through the agency's own fault is expressly not savings.
key_terms_explained.Augmentation: Using savings to top up an existing item. A non-existent project may never be funded this way.
key_terms_explained.PERA: Personnel Economic Relief Allowance — ₱2,000 a month for all Bangsamoro Government personnel, regular, contractual or casual.
key_terms_explained.RATA: Representation and Transportation Allowance — a monthly commutable allowance by rank.
key_terms_explained.EME: Extraordinary and Miscellaneous Expenses — an annual ceiling for meetings, official entertainment, public relations and similar costs.
key_terms_explained.Cash budgeting system: Appropriations valid for obligation only within a fixed window, after which they lapse and unobligated balances revert.
key_terms_explained.PhilGEPS: The Philippine Government Electronic Procurement System, the primary channel for all Bangsamoro procurement.
key_terms_explained.Special purpose funds: Central pots not assigned to a single agency — here including the Contingent Fund, Special Development Fund, Quick Response Fund and a Bangsamoro Support Fund to the Judiciary.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed and approved by the Chief Minister on the same day, 16 December 2025. Published by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management under the theme 'Building a Future-Ready Bangsamoro'.

for_citizens: None. An appropriations act imposes no duty on the public.
for_agencies: Remit fees, charges and revenues to the Bangsamoro Treasury unless expressly authorised to retain them, and post the schedule of fees on the website and prominently within the office
Secure prior clearance from the President for grants or donations from foreign governments or multilateral institutions
Obtain a Certification of Availability of Funds before incurring any obligation, and a Multi-Year Contractual Authority before any multi-year contract
Procure through PhilGEPS under RA 12009 and its 2025 implementing rules, and buy common-use supplies from the Procurement Service
Keep supply inventories within a 3-month requirement, with purchases beyond a year's requirement needing the Chief Minister's approval
Publish geo-tagged photos of infrastructure sites and submit quarterly implementation status reports
Formulate a Gender and Development Plan of at least 5% of the budget and submit it to the Bangsamoro Women Commission
Secure Office of the Chief Minister clearance for foreign travel at Salary Grade 25 and above, and report all foreign travel within 30 days
Answer Commission on Audit findings within 60 days and post the status report on the agency website
Submit financial and physical accountability reports monthly, quarterly or yearly, published on the agency website

what_is_prohibited: Using or retaining income without legal authority, or depositing income outside the Bangsamoro Treasury without legal basis — such disbursements are void.
Using revolving funds for discretionary and representation expenses.
Using any funds for partisan programmes, activities or projects, including voters education programmes.
Funding a non-existent activity or project by augmentation from savings or by using an appropriation in the act.
Declaring savings from allotments left unobligated through the agency's own fault, and proposing a discontinued project for funding in the next 2 fiscal years.
Granting a new cash advance before earlier ones are liquidated.
Sending an official to foreign training when they are due to retire within 1 year of the travel.
Granting transportation allowance to officials assigned to or actively using government vehicles.
Granting representation or transportation allowances above the rates fixed in the act.
Paying salaries, allowances, other benefits, or confidential and intelligence expenses from extraordinary and miscellaneous expense allocations.
Retaining or deducting fund releases as reserves or overhead except as authorised by law.
Altering, renovating or demolishing declared cultural property without the Chief Minister's prior approval on the heritage commission's recommendation.
Constructing a rainwater collection system on private lots or privately operated marketplaces.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence.
penalties.for_officials: Disbursements or expenditures made in violation of existing laws, rules and regulations are void, and any public official or employee who authorises, allows or permits them — or whose negligence results in them — is personally liable to the government for the full amount committed or expended, and subject to disciplinary action. Unauthorised use or retention of income, misuse of trust receipts or performance bonds, and violation of the mandatory expenditure rules all carry criminal and administrative liability. Failure to file financial and physical accountability reports automatically suspends the responsible officials' salaries until compliance, with repeated failure a ground for administrative disciplinary action. Unauthorised retirement benefits are void and must be refunded by the beneficiary, with those who authorised or connived in payment liable.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The ministry, office or agency implementing the programme or project
where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management; the Speaker; and Parliament's Committee on Finance, Budget and Management
where_to_complain.audit: The Commission on Audit, whose annual audit report each agency must answer within 60 days, with the status report posted publicly
where_to_complain.note: The Regional Project Monitoring and Evaluation Committee issues guidelines requiring agencies to report the status and percentage of completion of infrastructure projects on an official website.

everyday_scenarios: A resident wants proof a funded road was actually built. Section 21(d) requires agencies to publish geo-tagged photographs with stamps of the sites of all completed and ongoing infrastructure projects on their websites.
A government employee finds deductions have left them almost nothing. Section 47 provides that deductions may in no case reduce monthly net take-home pay below ₱5,000.

An employee in a Sulu provincial office wonders whether they will still be paid. Section 29 continues funding their salaries during the transition following Executive Order No. 91, and allows the same funds to cover retirement benefits and separation incentives.
A ministry wants to fund a new project mid-year from leftover money. Section 65 states that in no case shall a non-existent activity or project be funded by augmentation from savings.
An agency proposes a voters education programme. Section 60 prohibits funding partisan activities including voters education, and reverts any existing appropriation for them.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Appropriation of Funds. ₱114,077,644,141.90 is appropriated “out of the annual block grant, other subsidies from the National Government, share in the National Government taxes, fees, and charges collected in the Bangsamoro territorial jurisdiction, collections on regional taxes, fees, and charges, and unutilized prior years' appropriations” for the operation of the Bangsamoro Government from 1 January to 31 December 2026.

Bangsamoro Government Budget — The act is organised by agency: the Bangsamoro Transition Authority; the Office of the Chief Minister; and the ministries of Finance, and Budget and Management; Social Services and Development; Trade, Investments and Tourism; Labor and Employment; Transportation and Communications; Basic, Higher and Technical Education; Indigenous People's Affairs; Health; Public Works; the Interior and Local Government; Environment, Natural Resources and Energy; Human Settlements and Development; Science and Technology; Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reforms; and Public Order and Safety. Other executive offices funded are the Office of the Wali, the Bangsamoro Youth, Women and Sports Commissions, the Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, the Planning and Development Authority, the Attorney-General's Office, the Pilgrimage Authority, the Cooperatives and Social Enterprise Authority, the Development Academy of the Bangsamoro and the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission. Special purpose funds comprise Personnel Gratuity Funds, the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund, the Contingent Fund, the Special Development Fund, a Sustainable Assistance Mechanism for Local Moral Governance, a Bangsamoro Support Fund to the Judiciary, a Quick Response Fund, and an Infrastructure Modernization and Public Asset Construction and Transformation fund. The Bangsamoro Transition Authority receives ₱7,257,475,847, comprising General Administration and Support ₱2,100,320,735, Support to Operations ₱559,368,982, and Operations ₱4,597,786,130 — the latter split into a Legislation Program ₱1,706,586,130, a Representation Program ₱1,966,656,000, an Oversight Program ₱384,544,000, a Constituency Servicing Program ₱480,000,000, a Parliament Learning Program ₱40,000,000 and a Philippine Congress–Bangsamoro Parliament Forum ₱20,000,000.

Sections 2–14 (Receipts and Income) — The act itself serves as the allotment order except for appropriations with pre-release conditions and lump sums needing detail. Fees, charges and revenues are remitted to the Bangsamoro Treasury and form part of the General Fund, with exceptions: hospitals and health facilities remit 20% of income generated, motorised banca registration and licensing 50%, seaport charges 60%, and radio station licences and permits 60%. Foreign grants require prior clearance from the President. Trust receipts, performance bonds, public-private partnership receipts and revolving funds are each regulated, with revolving funds barred from paying discretionary and representation expenses. Special accounts, trust funds and unauthorised accounts must be closed and reverted in defined circumstances. Section 10 requires the Treasury to post publicly, on the finance ministry's website, information on all Special Accounts and funds including the agency, funding source, legal basis and allowable uses, with agency posts required to be searchable. National internal revenue taxes and import duties on foreign donations, grants and loans are deemed automatically appropriated. Loans and Official Development Assistance follow Section 24, Article XII of RA 11054 and Intergovernmental Fiscal Policy Board guidelines.

Sections 15–24 (Expenditure) — Procurement follows RA 12009, the New Government Procurement Act, and its 2025 implementing rules, with PhilGEPS as the primary channel; early procurement is authorised up to award; common-use supplies come from the Procurement Service; inventories are capped at a 3-month requirement. Motor vehicle purchases prioritise those critical to health and disaster response, and electric vehicle purchases must comply with the Electric Vehicle Industry Act. Infrastructure projects may not be sited in critical geohazard areas or no-build zones, must meet structural strength and climate resilience standards, must minimise biodiversity loss within the National Integrated Protected Area System, and require publication of geo-tagged photographs of all completed and ongoing project sites with quarterly status reports. Rainwater collection systems are required in public markets, school sites and government buildings. A Certification of Availability of Funds is required before any obligation, and a Multi-Year Contractual Authority before any multi-year contract.

Sections 25–40 (Cross-cutting programmes) — Every agency must formulate a Gender and Development Plan integrated into its regular activities amounting to at least 5% of its budget, with plans and accomplishment reports submitted to the Bangsamoro Women Commission and data passed to the Philippine Commission on Women. Agencies must address senior citizens and persons with disability, and all government infrastructure must include accessibility features. Section 29 provides provisional funding for Personnel Services of Sulu employees: agencies “shall continue to fund the salary requirements of the personnel in the provincial offices in Sulu until such time that a permanent funding mechanism or arrangement is established or until the end of the fiscal year, whichever comes earlier”, in line with Executive Order No. 91 declaring the Province of Sulu part of Region IX (Zamboanga Peninsula), with such funds not to be declared as savings and available to fund retirement benefits and separation incentives. Section 30 encourages all agencies to integrate and mainstream Islamic or Shari'ah-compliant finance, with the Chief Minister to promulgate guidelines on the recommendation of the Technical Working Group on Islamic Finance. Further sections cover protection of built heritage, disaster risk reduction and climate adaptation with multi-scenario probabilistic analysis, disaster risk budget tagging, energy efficiency, multi-hazard early warning systems, biodiversity protection, green practices, seismic retrofitting, materials recovery facilities and alternative dispute resolution.

Sections 41–57 (Personnel Benefits) — Personnel Services for one fiscal year “shall not exceed forty-five percent (45%) of the total revenue sources of the Bangsamoro Government” under Section 6, Article XII of RA 11054. Annual extraordinary expenses are capped at ₱264,000 for the Chief Minister, ₱108,000 for each Deputy Chief Minister, the Speaker and Members of Parliament, ₱45,600 for each Minister, ₱26,400 for each Deputy Minister and Director-General, and ₱19,200 for each Director II or III, with a further ₱90,000 in miscellaneous expenses per office — none of which may pay salaries, allowances, other benefits or confidential and intelligence expenses. Monthly representation and transportation allowances are ₱15,500 for the Chief Minister, ₱12,500 for Deputy Chief Ministers, the Speaker and Members of Parliament, ₱10,000 for Ministers, ₱9,500 for Deputy Ministers and Directors-General, ₱8,500 for Directors II and III, and ₱6,000 for Division Chiefs and Directors I. Deductions may not reduce monthly net take-home pay below ₱5,000. PERA is ₱2,000 a month; uniform or clothing allowance up to ₱7,000 a year; medical allowance up to ₱7,000 a year for HMO-type benefits; a mid-year bonus of 1 month's basic salary; a year-end bonus of 1 month plus a ₱5,000 cash gift. Government lawyers receive ₱5,000 per court appearance, capped at 50% of monthly basic salary and not payable before quasi-judicial or administrative agencies. Honoraria are limited to defined categories, with special project honoraria capped at 25% of annual basic salary. Unauthorised retirement benefits are void and refundable.

Sections 58–72 (Release and Use of Funds) — Appropriations are available for release and obligation until 31 December 2027, with Personnel Services valid only until 31 December 2026 and an extended payment period to 31 March 2027; disbursement is generally due by 31 December 2027, with infrastructure completion, inspection and payment and delivery of other items by 30 June 2028. After the validity period unreleased appropriations, unobligated allotments and obligated allotments for undelivered goods or incomplete works revert to the Treasury for reappropriation under Section 19, Article XII of RA 11054 — except that “the Share of the Constituent Local Government Units in taxes, fees, and charges collected within the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region shall be available until fully released, obligated, and disbursed”. No retention or deduction of releases as reserves or overhead is permitted. Section 60 prohibits all funding for partisan programmes, activities or projects, including voters education programmes, and reverts any existing appropriation for them whether obligated or unobligated. The Chief Minister and the Speaker may each declare and use savings within their own appropriations, reporting semestrally and annually to Parliament with the reports posted on their websites. Savings arise only from completion, final discontinuance or abandonment, or from improved systems and efficiencies — allotments left unobligated through the agency's own fault are not savings, and a discontinued project may not be proposed for funding in the next 2 fiscal years. In no case may a non-existent activity or project be funded by augmentation. Cash advances may not be granted until earlier ones are liquidated, with an annual report on cash advances naming recipients submitted jointly by the agency head and the Commission on Audit auditor. Officials who authorise, allow or permit unlawful expenditure, or whose negligence results in it, are personally liable for the full amount.

Sections 73–83 (Administrative Procedures and Final) — Agencies must review their mandates and identify where resources should be rechannelled, with the finance ministry able to recommend creation, abolition, renaming, consolidation or merger of bureaus and offices and the reclassification or transfer of positions. The Chief Minister is authorised to create new offices, modify the organisational structure of executive agencies, and create or modify positions whenever public interest requires. Foreign travel by officials at Salary Grade 25 and above requires clearance from the Office of the Chief Minister, with all foreign travel reported within 30 days and Members of Parliament reporting to the Committee on Accounts. Agencies retaining income outside the Treasury must publish audited financial statements and narrative reports. Commission on Audit findings must be answered within 60 days and the status report posted online. Financial and physical accountability reports must be published, with failure automatically suspending the responsible officials' salaries. Infrastructure transparency requires publication of contract details within 30 days and actual costs within 30 days of completion, with the Regional Project Monitoring and Evaluation Committee promulgating further guidelines. Public funds appropriated under the act are exempt from garnishment, levy and execution. The act takes effect on 1 January 2026.

related_legislation.related_note: Funding sources and the 45% Personnel Services ceiling derive from Sections 6, 19 and 24 of Article XII of RA 11054, the Organic Law. Remittance of agency income follows Book VII of BAA 13, the Administrative Code, with specific retention rates drawn from its Title XV. Procurement follows RA 12009 and alternative dispute resolution Book V, Chapter 9 of BAA 13. Gender and development follows RA 9710, the Magna Carta of Women, and reports flow to the Bangsamoro Women Commission created by BAA 8. Section 29 gives effect to Executive Order No. 91 declaring the Province of Sulu part of Region IX. BAA 84, the Bangsamoro Budget System Act of 2025, codifies as permanent law many of the rules this act carries annually.

display_header.line2: General Appropriations Act of the Bangsamoro, FY 2026
display_header.what_this_does: Appropriates ₱114.08 billion for 2026 and sets the rules on how every peso may be spent.
display_header.who_it_affects: Everyone in the region · all government personnel · contractors · constituent LGUs

views.simple: The region's ₱114.08 billion budget for 2026, drawn from the block grant, national tax shares, regional taxes and unspent prior-year money. Beyond the allocations it carries 83 sections of operating rules: Personnel Services capped at 45% of revenue, at least 5% of every agency budget for gender programmes, a ban on funding partisan activities including voters education, geo-tagged photographs of every infrastructure site published online, rainwater collection systems in public buildings, continued salary funding for Sulu provincial staff following Executive Order No. 91, an Islamic finance mainstreaming framework, a ₱5,000 net take-home pay floor, and automatic salary suspension for officials who fail to report.
views.official: AN ACT APPROPRIATING FUNDS FOR THE OPERATION OF THE BANGSAMORO GOVERNMENT FROM JANUARY ONE TO DECEMBER THIRTY-ONE, TWO THOUSAND TWENTY-SIX AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

provenance.source: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 85, enacted text as signed and published by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management. Pages 1–6 and 320–349 of 349 were read; see reading_scope under implementation status for what was not.
provenance.generation: Grand total and General Provisions transcribed from the enacted text on 19 August 2026. Agency line items other than the Bangsamoro Transition Authority's were not read. Verify against the official copy before citing.
